newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.N. approves additional France-Iraq wheat sales.
newsitem.headline: U.N. approves additional France-Iraq wheat sales.

text.p: The United Nations has approved the sale of a total of 450,000 tonnes of French soft wheat to Iraq under a U.N. monitored oil-for-food pact, a French government source said on Monday.
The previous count on May 12 showed the total at 400,000 tonnes.
Traders have sold a total of 625,000 tonnes of French wheat to Iraq since December, when Iraq started selling oil to raise funds to buy humanitarian supplies.
U.N. approval for a remaining 175,000 tonnes of French wheat is still pending, the source said.
But because the wheat was to be delivered to Iraq in April at the latest, the U.N clearance may come too late for some exporters.
Last week, exporters said they feared that over 200,000 tonnes of French exports may be at risk.

Iraqi authorities and trade houses are however trying to work out a solution, including allowing shipments to take place during the next season now that the EU's wheat export season is virtually over.
But it remains unclear if the European Union will accept that idea, which may also require higher export refunds, one exporter said.
Before the sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, Iraq was the world's number six wheat buyer, with imports of 3.7 million tonnes in 1989/90.
